entries.rule: efficacy: did the trial's primary endpoint respond; a secondary endpoint governs only with endpoint_role poc_gate
entries.note: Brentjens 2013 full text: 'The primary endpoint of this study is safety of CAR modified T cell infusion' (NCT01044069); endpoint_role 'primary' is wrong. ROCKET (NCT02535364, CR primary) stopped for deaths, efficacy unreported. untested_reason unsettled.
entries.adjudication_note: Efficacy rule: the trial's primary endpoint governs; NCT01044069's primary was safety, no poc_gate, and house style (SAPHIRA1) leaves such trials unscored. ROCKET's CR primary went unreported after deaths: untested_reason unsettled (rule 5).

entries.note: Kantarjian 2016 (PMID 26775883): primary endpoint ORR, 25.5% at selected dose, study stopped early; quote verbatim. Contra over partial-same is defensible against near-universal xenograft responses.
SBRA quote verbatim (MCL review); model_filed true is supported for the BLA.

ZUMA-3 Lancet 2021 (PMID 34097852) primary endpoint overall CR/CRi, quote verbatim; model_src Kochenderfer 2010 Blood (PMID 20631379) is the murine-CD19 CAR paper. Lymphoma-model-to-ALL transfer flagged by drafter.
Quote is about homing, not safety, but untested/no_prediction is right: SCID mice cannot show CRS or cerebral edema.

Quote verbatim. Partial same is defensible: 10 mg/kg weekly in mice (~30 mg/m2) is below 70/90 mg/m2. But confidence_note is wrong: the ALL trial did assess ocular AEs (9 grade 1/2) and 3 neuropathies.

entries.rule: Evidence rule 1: a trial paper that merely cites the model paper is a pairing (comparison_stated: false, model_src named)
entries.note: Quote verbatim (PMC11456753). Ma 2024 only cites the preclinical work (ref 23) without mouse numbers: set comparison_stated false, model_src Kang 2020 (tier 1). Infusions Dec 2015-Feb 2019 predate the mouse paper; post hoc, non-randomized: lower confidence.
entries.adjudication_note: Evidence rule 1: Ma 2024 only cites the mouse work, so a pairing (comparison_stated false, model_src Kang 2020); status stays same. Not retro: no patient CRS comparison was public before Kang 2020 (rule 7).

missing: JCAR015 ROCKET phase 2 (NCT02535364): halted Jul 2016 and terminated Mar 2017 after 5 cerebral-edema deaths (Juno press releases; AJMC/BioPharma Dive; PMID 29208604). Not a scorable mouse miss (SCID mice cannot show it), but the trial outcome belongs in a dated safety note on the nalm6 track.

CRS/neurotoxicity mouse models built with the class's own CAR: Giavridis 2018 Nat Med (doi:10.1038/s41591-018-0041-7; 19-28z CAR T in SCID-beige, IL-1/IL-6 CRS) and Norelli 2018 Nat Med (doi:10.1038/s41591-018-0036-4; humanized mice, CRS and neurotoxicity). Both reproduce known patient CRS, so they would be retrodiction tracks (retro) for safety.
Davila 2014 Sci Transl Med (doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.3008226; 16 adults, 19-28z, 88% CR) is an intermediate patient source for the nalm6 track (no status change).
No data were searched or shown for members TBI-1501, BinD19 or 'CD19 CAR-T with CRS suppression technology'; not verified by checker either.
rule_questions: A phase 1 trial whose primary endpoint is safety and whose only efficacy readout is a secondary (CR/MRD) with no poc_gate designation: does efficacy stay untested (strict reading, as proposed for efficacy 4) or can a single-arm phase 1 count its response readout?

Engagement for a cell-depleting class: is clearance of the target-bearing malignant cells (MRD) an engagement readout at all, given it is also the efficacy endpoint, or should engagement use normal B-cell aplasia?

Safety for an ADC track where the mouse tolerability study dosed below the human-equivalent of the clinical dose: does 'no obvious side effects' count as a stated prediction (scorable same/contra) or as no_prediction?

A nonclinical package filed for one indication (Tecartus MCL SBRA) and carried to another (B-ALL supplement): should model_filed be true for the second indication without the supplement review being opened?

safety 11 (nsg-raji-ssCART19-il6kd): all patient infusions (Dec 2015-Feb 2019) preceded Kang 2020 submission (Mar 2020), but the ssCART-vs-cCART comparison was first analysed post hoc in 2024 and the mouse run date is not stated. Is a model published after patients were dosed, but before the comparative result was analysed, prospective (same) or retro?
